title: Preparing a Debate Outline
text:
A debate outline helps a speaker organize their ideas before the event. It usually starts with a clear statement of the main claim. Then it lists the reasons that support the claim, and each reason is followed by evidence such as facts or examples.

Many students forget to plan for the other side. A good outline also includes possible counterarguments and short answers to them. Speakers who prepare these responses feel more confident and can respond calmly when the opponent speaks.

questions.text: What does a debate outline usually start with?
options: A clear statement of the main claim
A short answer to an opponent

questions.text: According to the passage, what do many students forget to plan for?
What can be inferred about a speaker who has no prepared responses to counterarguments?
options: They will probably feel unprepared when challenged
They will always win the debate
They do not need any evidence
They will speak for a shorter time

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain how to win every debate
To describe the steps of preparing a debate outline
To argue that students should avoid debates

vocabulary.definition: a plan or summary of the main points
a statement that something is true
facts or examples that support an idea
arguments that oppose a point of view

paragraph_translations: Um esboço de debate ajuda o orador a organizar suas ideias antes do evento. Normalmente ele começa com uma declaração clara da principal afirmação. Em seguida, lista as razões que apoiam a afirmação, e cada razão é seguida de provas, como fatos ou exemplos.

Muitos estudantes esquecem de planejar o lado oposto. Um bom esboço também inclui possíveis contra-argumentos e respostas curtas para eles. Oradores que preparam essas respostas se sentem mais confiantes e conseguem responder com calma quando o adversário fala.
